sections.h2: Who records deeds in Fayette County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
The Fayette County Clerk's Land Records department does. It sits in Room 132 at 162 East Main Street in Lexington, and the number to call is 859-253-3344. Copies and inquiries are handled from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, while the recording window closes at 4:00 p.m., so a closing package that arrives at 4:15 waits for the next business day.

The clerk's is a constitutional office whose duties come from the Kentucky Revised Statutes. Besides recording, it prepares property tax bills, runs elections and titles vehicles. Fayette was one of the three original counties created in 1780, and its land records reach back to about 1792, the year Kentucky became a state. They exist in books, on microfilm and as digital images.

For a seller, the clerk is the last stop on a sale. The deed is signed at the closing table, the transfer tax is paid, and recording makes the buyer's ownership part of the public record. Most of the paperwork rides along with the closing agent, but knowing the rules helps when a deed is signed outside a title office.

sections.h2: What formatting rules does the Fayette County Clerk enforce on deeds?
sections.html:
The Kentucky County Clerks Association adopted the Property Records Industry Association standards for real estate documents on January 1, 2020, and Fayette applies them. A document that breaks the rules can be turned away at the desk, so check the layout before the signing appointment.

  • Paper: 20 lb white stock with no watermarks, 8.5 by 11 inches preferred and 8.5 by 14 accepted, printed on one side only.
  • Margins: a 3 inch blank top margin on the first page for the recorder's stamp, and 1 inch on every other edge.
  • Text: 10-point Times New Roman or similar, no more than nine lines per inch, in black ink with dark blue signatures.
  • No staples or binding, no colored highlighter marks and no embossed seals unless inked.

The clerk's recording list is wide. It covers deeds, quitclaim deeds, easements, powers of attorney, land contracts, affidavits of descent or heirship, mortgages, releases, lis pendens notices, judgment and mechanic's liens, and wills. A deed in lieu of foreclosure, a deed correcting an earlier deed or an heir's affidavit all travel through the same desk.

sections.h2: How do I get a deed to the Fayette County Clerk?
sections.html:
There are four routes, and the clerk's office has set a different cutoff for each. Walking documents in during recording desk hours is the oldest of them. The recording desk takes documents in person from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays.

  • E-recording: the office accepts submissions through CSC, ePN, Simplifile and Hopdox, the channels title companies already use.
  • Mail or courier: send documents by US Mail, UPS or FedEx to Fayette County Clerk, 162 E. Main Street, Room 132, Lexington, KY 40507.
  • Drop box: a box in the Helix Garage, near the second-floor entrance to the clerk's office and to the right of the yellow garage fee kiosk, takes envelopes from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. The last pickup of the day is at 4:00 p.m., and documents must be sealed in envelopes.
  • In person: the clerk's window, Room 132.

Veterans can have a DD-214 discharge recorded at the clerk's office at no charge and receive a copy without a fee. Those records are closed to the public, so copies require photo identification and, in some cases, a birth certificate.

sections.h2: What does the Fayette County Clerk charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
State law sets the recording fee, and a deed of up to five pages costs $33. KRS 64.012, in the version that took effect July 15, 2026, lists the rest of the schedule, and the clerk adds its own copy charges. The clerk also publishes a fee schedule for e-recording, so ask for the current sheet before closing.

Mail requests add $1.00 for postage and handling, and mailing a plat copy commonly costs $2.00. Copy requests by mail go on the clerk's form with payment, no more than two requests per form, and the office aims to fill them within three business days. The statute also lets the clerk collect a $10 reimbursement for permanent record storage on deeds, plats and mortgages. Cash, credit cards or checks are accepted at the window for copy fees.

sections.h2: How does Kentucky's transfer tax work on a Fayette County sale?
sections.html:
The grantor pays $0.50 for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, declared in the deed. KRS 142.050 requires the county clerk to compute the tax and collect it before accepting the deed for recording. For a sale, the value is the full price including any liens on the property, and for a gift it is the estimated open-market price.

A house that sells for $293,500, the Census median owner-occupied value for the county, produces 587 blocks of $500 and a tax of $293.50. A $250,000 sale produces $250.00. The clerk keeps 5 percent of what it collects as a collection fee and passes the rest to the county treasurer every three months for the county general fund.

The statute lists exemptions, among them transfers between spouses or former spouses in a divorce, transfers between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild for nominal consideration, deeds under foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure, sales for delinquent taxes, partitions, and deeds that confirm or correct an earlier deed. A clerk who records a taxable deed without collecting the tax faces a $50 fine for each offense.

sections.h2: How can I search Fayette County land records and guard my title?
sections.html:
Use fayettedeeds.com, the clerk's online portal. Land records from 1970 to the present can be searched, viewed and printed there, and many earlier records sit in the non-indexed documents section. All plats have been digitized. Since January 3, 2022, the clerk has indexed documents exactly as written on the document instead of using its older abbreviation list, so searching a few spelling variations is wise.

The clerk's free Recording Notification Service sends an email each time a document is recorded against a name or address you register, up to 10 items per email address. It is sometimes called a fraud alert, and the clerk cautions that it gives no guarantee of catching every filing.

  • Check the portal now and then for anything recorded in your name or against your property.
  • Look often at vacant property to be sure no one is occupying it unlawfully.
  • Give the PVA and the sheriff your correct mailing address so tax bills and notices reach you.
  • If fraud is suspected, call the Lexington Police Department at 859-258-3600 and a lawyer. The clerk cannot remove a recorded document without a court order.

The same office collects delinquent real property taxes once the sheriff passes them on after April 15, takes only cash, money order or cashier's or certified check, and searches delinquent bills on fayettedeeds.com. The 2026 delinquent tax sale was held on July 24 at 11:00 a.m.

sections.h2: What should a seller in Fayette County know about the local market?
sections.html:
Fayette County is a consolidated city-county government, so one office, the clerk, serves all of Lexington's recording needs. The Census Bureau counts 139,715 households, with 2.23 people per household, and 79.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $1,636 a month in housing costs, against $599 for owners without one, and median gross rent is $1,164.

Those numbers describe a steady market, but a house in poor repair or with a title tangle can still stall on the open market. A closing that depends on a late-found lien or a missing heir's affidavit may be easier to resolve with a cash buyer, who can accept the house as-is while the title issue is cleared at the recording desk.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Fayette County?
faqs.a: Record it with the Fayette County Clerk's Land Records department, Room 132 at 162 East Main Street in Lexington. You can walk it in, mail it, use the Helix Garage drop box or e-record through an approved vendor.

faqs.q: What time does the Fayette County Clerk stop recording documents?
faqs.a: The recording window closes at 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, even though the office answers copy requests and inquiries until 4:30 p.m. The drop box's last pickup is also 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Fayette County house sale?
faqs.a: It is $0.50 per $500 of value, paid by the seller as grantor. A $293,500 sale produces a $293.50 tax, which the clerk collects before recording.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Fayette County deed online?
faqs.a: Yes. Search fayettedeeds.com for land records from 1970 to the present, plus many older records in the non-indexed section. Plats are all online, and certified marriage records can be ordered there.

faqs.q: Does the Fayette County Clerk collect unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, once the sheriff transfers a delinquent bill after April 15. Pay the clerk in full with cash, money order or a cashier's or certified check, and call 859-254-4941 for County Attorney payment arrangements.
